english.title: Possess for sale live Schedule 1 wild bird or egg
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), had in your possession for the purpose of sale

(A)_[a live wild bird]_
(B)_[live wild birds]_
(C)_[a wild bird's egg or any part thereof]_
(D)_[a wild bird's eggs or any part thereof]_
(E)_[wild birds' eggs or any part thereof]_

included in Schedule 1 to the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, namely **(..SPECIFY SPECIES OF BIRD(S)..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 6(1)(a), 6(4) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

english.notes:
(i) Does not apply to birds listed in Part I of Schedule 3 to the Act.
(ii) See Section 27 for meaning of "sale" and "wild bird".
(iii) See Section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
(iv) See Section 21(7) for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(v) As amended by paragraph 10 of Schedule 12 to the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000
(vi) See also offence wordings H4586, H4587 and H4589.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Where more than one bird or egg is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each bird or egg (Section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
